conviction_note: The findings sum to +0.6. Two of them lean positive: every data-centre and electrical peer that reported after Legrand's own consensus was collected (5-9 Oct) beat and raised, and Rexel, Legrand's main distributor, printed Europe +4.5%. Two lean slightly negative: the FY consensus already sits at the top of the +8-10% organic guide, and a quant fund has opened a short. The scaled number lands on the same +0.6, but by a different route: abs 6.0 x (2 x 0.55 - 1). p_up is held near 50 because Legrand's nine-month print has fallen four years running (-5.4, -1.3, -7.3, -12.2) and its 2026 beats were sold (-1.7, -0.35). The sizes are proxy evidence on a 17-analyst mega-cap, so all of them stay small.

findings.finding: Every data-centre and electrical-equipment peer that reported after Legrand's consensus was collected (5-9 Oct) beat and raised. Schneider (16 Oct): organic +16.9%, beating its own company consensus, with 'triple-digit demand growth' in data centres, guidance raised. Vertiv (28 Oct): organic orders over +100%, guidance raised. nVent (30 Oct): organic +44%, guidance raised. Eaton (3 Nov): Electrical Americas +22%, book-to-bill 1.3. Against that, Legrand's Q3 bar of about +10.7% organic is a two-year stack of ~17.4 points (Q3 2025 was +6.7%) versus ~20.5 in Q2, so consensus assumes a slowdown on an easy comp.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 6 Nov 2025 Q3 organic came in at +6.7% against an Oddo-cited +8.7%, with N&C America +13.3%, 4.8pts below consensus, and the stock fell 12.2%. On 7 May 2026 a Q1 beat was followed by -1.7%. On 29 Jul 2026 an H1 beat plus a guidance raise was followed by -0.35%. Misses on this line have been punished and beats ignored.
findings.why_not_priced: Legrand's published bar was collected before any of these prints. The tape has gone the other way: LR fell from 148.40 (6 Oct) to 131 and Schneider from 272.8 to 237. If the peer read-across were priced, LR would have held up against its peers rather than de-rating with the AI-capex trade. Caveat: peer beats did not lift those stocks either (Schneider 'little moved' on its print), and sell-side whisper numbers have probably risen above the 9 Oct figure.

All are competitors, not counterparties, so they count as one proxy finding.

findings.finding: Rexel, Legrand's largest distributor, reported Q3 2026 sales of +11.4% at constant days on 22 Oct, against a 6.6% consensus. Its Europe rose +4.5% (France +3.6%, DACH +6.4%) and its US +18.2%, with data-centre sales growing at triple digits. Legrand's consensus implies Q3 Europe only around -0.6% (9M -1.8% after H1 -2.4%), and Legrand's own Europe was -2.0% in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q3 2025 Europe came in at +2.7% against 1.8% expected, but that beat was swamped by the North America miss and the stock fell 12.2%. Europe is a secondary line for this stock (about 35% of sales).

findings.why_not_priced: The Legrand consensus PDF predates Rexel's print by two weeks, and its Europe line (-1.8% for 9M) has not been updated in public. Caveats, already applied to the size: part of Rexel's growth is copper-cable price inflation that Legrand does not share, and Legrand faces a tough Europe comp (+2.7% in Q3 2025).

A narrowing to the top end is therefore already in the bar. Only a guide above 10%, or margin guidance above 20.7%, is news.

findings.why_not_priced: This is the bar itself: the risk that a 'raise' turns out to be a non-event. The stock's 11% de-rating since 6 Oct lowers how much the price needs. That is why this finding is small rather than large.

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly positive against a negative sealed lean (-0.35, short building) and a -7.4% 20-day run-up. That run-up is a sector de-rating shared with Schneider, not Legrand news, and it lowers the bar in price. The reaction history (nine-month prints sold four years running, 2026 beats sold) cuts against the positive lean, so p_up stays at 55.
language_note: The Q3 2025 comp (organic +6.7% against an Oddo-cited +8.7%, N&C America +13.3%, 4.8pts below consensus, Europe +2.7%) and the reason for the 12% fall came from the French BFM Bourse article. The English searches returned the release headline, not the miss against the bar.
Rexel's Q3 country split (France +3.6%, DACH +6.4%, Europe +4.5%) came only from French coverage (Idéal Investisseur / BFM). The English search did not surface the distributor read at all.
The current per-holder short positions (CFM since 27/10, Sandbar 0.49%) came from ABC Bourse's French mirror of the AMF register.
Legrand's own consensus PDFs, the H1 release and the CMD release are in English and carried the bar.
lessons_applied: 'You were right about the number and too small about the move' and 'the move is in the guide': abs_move_pct raised from 5.0 to 6.0. A guidance change (narrowing or raise) is likely, the Q3 numbers are new, and this name's own nine-month prints average about 6.5% in absolute terms.

'A verified fact is not a predicted reaction' and 'a narrow proxy loses to a broad series': the peer finding is from competitors, not counterparties, and peers' own beats were not rewarded, so it was cut from +1.0 to +0.8.
'Let the reaction history move p_up, not abs_move_pct': p_up cut from 56 to 55 for nine-month prints sold four years running and 2026 beats sold.
The pre-release rule does not apply: no Q3 trading update or information privilégiée was found.
